column3: Black: They shoot paralyzing liquid from their head bumps. They use vibration to hurt their opponents.\n\nWhite: It increases the power of its punches by vibrating the bumps on its fists. It can turn a boulder to rubble with one punch.

Black: When it tightens its belt, it becomes stronger. Wild Throh use vines to weave their own belts.\n\nWhite: When they encounter foes bigger than themselves, they try to throw them. They always travel in packs of five.

Black: The sound of Sawk punching boulders and trees can be heard all the way from the mountains where they train.\n\nWhite: Tying their belts gets them pumped and makes their punches more destructive. Disturbing their training angers them.

Black: Leavanny dress it in clothes they made for it when it hatched. It hides its head in its hood while it is sleeping.\n\nWhite: This Pokémon makes clothes for itself. It chews up leaves and sews them with sticky thread extruded from its mouth.

Black: Forests where Swadloon live have superb foliage because the nutrients they make from fallen leaves nourish the plant life.\n\nWhite: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.

Black: Upon finding a small Pokémon, it weaves clothing for it from leaves, using the cutters on its arms and sticky silk.\n\nWhite: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.

Black: Its bite injects a potent poison, enough to paralyze large bird Pokémon that try to prey on it.\n\nWhite: It discovers what is going on around it by using the feelers on its head and tail. It is brutally aggressive.

Black: Protected by a hard shell, it spins its body like a wheel and crashes furiously into its enemies.\n\nWhite: It is usually motionless, but when attacked, it rotates at high speed and then crashes into its opponent.

Black: With quick movements, it chases down its foes, attacking relentlessly with its horns until it prevails.\n\nWhite: Highly aggressive, it uses the claws near its neck to dig into its opponents and poison them.

column2: Abundant Shrine, Lostlorn Forest, Pinwheel Forest
column3: Black: When attacked, it escapes by shooting cotton from its body. The cotton serves as a decoy to distract the attacker.\n\nWhite: They go wherever the wind takes them. On rainy days, their bodies are heavier, so they take shelter beneath big trees.

column2: Abundant Shrine, Lostlorn Forest, Pinwheel Forest
column3: Black: Like the wind, it can slip through any gap, no matter how small. It leaves balls of white fluff behind.\n\nWhite: Riding whirlwinds, they appear. These Pokémon sneak through gaps into houses and cause all sorts of mischief.

Black: The leaves on its head are very bitter. Eating one of these leaves is known to refresh a tired body.\n\nWhite: Since they prefer moist, nutrient-rich soil, the areas where Petilil live are known to be good for growing plants.

Black: Even veteran Trainers face a challenge in getting its beautiful flower to bloom. This Pokémon is popular with celebrities.\n\nWhite: The fragrance of the garland on its head has a relaxing effect. It withers if a Trainer does not take good care of it.

column2: Route 1, 3, 6, 11, 14, Dragonspiral Tower, Abundant Shrine, Giant Chasm, Driftveil City, Lostlorn Forest, Wellspring Cave, Striaton City, Challenger's Cave, Victory Road, Village Bridge, Pinwheel Forest
column3: Black: Red and blue Basculin get along so poorly, they’ll start fighting instantly. These Pokémon are very hostile.\n\nWhite: Red and blue Basculin usually do not get along, but sometimes members of one school mingle with the other’s school.

Black: They live buried in the sands of the desert. The sun-warmed sands prevent their body temperature from dropping.\n\nWhite: It moves along below the sand’s surface, except for its nose and eyes. A dark membrane shields its eyes from the sun.

Black: They live in groups of a few individuals. Protective membranes shield their eyes from sandstorms.\n\nWhite: The special membrane covering its eyes can sense the heat of objects, so it can see its surroundings even in darkness.

Black: They never allow prey to escape. Their jaws are so powerful, they can crush the body of an automobile.\n\nWhite: It can expand the focus of its eyes, enabling it to see objects in the far distance as if it were using binoculars.

Black: When its internal fire is burning, it cannot calm down and it runs around. When the fire diminishes, it falls asleep.\n\nWhite: Darumaka’s droppings are hot, so people used to put them in their clothes to keep themselves warm.

Black: Its internal fire burns at 2,500° F, making enough power that it can destroy a dump truck with one punch.\n\nWhite: When weakened in battle, it transforms into a stone statue. Then it sharpens its mind and fights on mentally.

Black: It uses an up-tempo song and dance to drive away the bird Pokémon that prey on its flower seeds.\n\nWhite: Arid regions are their habitat. They move rhythmically, making a sound similar to maracas.

Black: This Pokémon can easily melt holes in hard rocks with a liquid secreted from its mouth.\n\nWhite: It makes a hole in a suitable rock. If that rock breaks, the Pokémon remains agitated until it locates a replacement.

Black: Competing for territory, Crustle fight viciously. The one whose boulder is broken is the loser of the battle.\n\nWhite: It possesses legs of enormous strength, enabling it to carry heavy slabs for many days, even when crossing arid land.

Black: Its skin has a rubbery elasticity, so it can reduce damage by defensively pulling its skin up to its neck.\n\nWhite: It immediately headbutts anyone that makes eye contact with it. Its skull is massively thick.

Black: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.\n\nWhite: It can smash concrete blocks with its kicking attacks. The one with the biggest crest is the group leader.

Black: They never vary the route they fly, because their memories of guarding an ancient city remain steadfast.\n\nWhite: The guardians of an ancient city, they use their psychic power to attack enemies that invade their territory.

Black: Each of them carries a mask that used to be its face when it was human. Sometimes they look at it and cry.\n\nWhite: These Pokémon arose from the spirits of people interred in graves in past ages. Each retains memories of its former life.

Black: It has been said that they swallow those who get too close and turn them into mummies. They like to eat gold nuggets.\n\nWhite: They pretend to be elaborate coffins to teach lessons to grave robbers. Their bodies are covered in pure gold.

Black: Restored from a fossil, this Pokémon can dive to depths beyond half a mile.\n\nWhite: About 100 million years ago, these Pokémon swam in oceans. It is thought they also went on land to attack prey.

Black: They can live both in the ocean and on land. A slap from one of them is enough to open a hole in the bottom of a tanker.\n\nWhite: Incredible jaw strength enables them to chew up steel beams and rocks along with their prey.

Black: Said to be an ancestor of bird Pokémon, they were unable to fly and moved about by hopping from one branch to another.\n\nWhite: Revived from a fossil, this Pokémon is thought to be the ancestor of all bird Pokémon.

Black: They are intelligent and will cooperate to catch prey. From the ground, they use a running start to take flight.\n\nWhite: It runs better than it flies. It catches prey by running at speeds comparable to those of an automobile.

Black: Inhaling the gas they belch will make you sleep for a week. They prefer unsanitary places.\n\nWhite: The combination of garbage bags and industrial waste caused the chemical reaction that created this Pokémon.

Black: It clenches opponents with its left arm and finishes them off with foul-smelling poison gas belched from its mouth.\n\nWhite: They absorb garbage and make it part of their bodies. They shoot a poisonous liquid from their right-hand fingertips.

Black: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.\n\nWhite: To protect themselves from danger, they hide their true identities by transforming into people and Pokémon.

Black: Bonds between these Pokémon are very strong. It protects the safety of its pack by tricking its opponents.\n\nWhite: Each has the ability to fool a large group of people simultaneously. They protect their lair with illusory scenery.

Black: They greet one another by rubbing each other with their tails, which are always kept well groomed and clean.\n\nWhite: These Pokémon prefer a tidy habitat. They are always sweeping and dusting, using their tails as brooms.

Black: Their white fur is coated in a special oil that makes it easy for them to deflect attacks.\n\nWhite: Their white fur feels amazing to touch. Their fur repels dust and prevents static electricity from building up.

Black: Their ribbonlike feelers increase their psychic power. They are always staring at something.\n\nWhite: They intently observe both Trainers and Pokémon. Apparently, they are looking at something that only Gothita can see.

Black: They use hypnosis to control people and Pokémon. Tales of Gothorita leading people astray are told in every corner.\n\nWhite: Starlight is the source of their power. At night, they mark star positions by using psychic power to float stones.

Black: Starry skies thousands of light-years away are visible in the space distorted by their intense psychic power.\n\nWhite: They can predict the future from the placement and movement of the stars. They can see Trainers’ life spans.

Black: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.\n\nWhite: Because their bodies are enveloped in a special liquid, they can survive in any environment.

Black: Since they have two divided brains, at times they suddenly try to take two different actions at once.\n\nWhite: When their brains, now divided in two, are thinking the same thoughts, these Pokémon exhibit their maximum power.

Black: When Reuniclus shake hands, a network forms between their brains, increasing their psychic power.\n\nWhite: These remarkably intelligent Pokémon fight by controlling arms that can grip with rock-crushing power.

Black: These bird Pokémon are excellent divers. They swim around in the water eating their favorite food--peat moss.\n\nWhite: When attacked, it uses its feathers to splash water, escaping under cover of the spray.

Black: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.\n\nWhite: It administers sharp, powerful pecks with its bill. It whips its long neck to deliver forceful repeated strikes.

Black: The temperature of their breath is -58° F. They create snow crystals and make snow fall in the areas around them.\n\nWhite: This Pokémon formed from icicles bathed in energy from the morning sun. It sleeps buried in snow.

Black: Snowy mountains are this Pokémon’s habitat. During an ancient ice age, they moved to southern areas.\n\nWhite: It conceals itself from enemy eyes by creating many small ice particles and hiding among them.

Black: Swallowing large amounts of water, they make snow clouds inside their bodies and attack their foes with violent blizzards.\n\nWhite: If both heads get angry simultaneously, this Pokémon expels a blizzard, burying everything in snow.

Black: The color and scent of their fur changes to match the mountain grass. When they sense hostility, they hide in the grass.\n\nWhite: The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon’s fur. People use it to mark the seasons.

Black: They migrate according to the seasons. People can tell the season by looking at Sawsbuck’s horns.\n\nWhite: The plants growing on its horns change according to the season. The leaders of the herd possess magnificent horns.

column2: Route 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, Dragonspiral Tower, Abundant Shrine, Lostlorn Forest, Village Bridge
column3: Black: The energy made in its cheeks’ electric pouches is stored inside its membrane and released while it is gliding.\n\nWhite: They live on treetops and glide using the inside of a cape-like membrane while discharging electricity.

Black: These mysterious Pokémon evolve when they receive electrical stimulation while they are in the same place as Shelmet.\n\nWhite: When they feel threatened, they spit an acidic liquid to drive attackers away. This Pokémon targets Shelmet.

Black: They fly around at high speed, striking with their pointed spears. Even when in trouble, they face opponents bravely.\n\nWhite: These Pokémon evolve by wearing the shell covering of a Shelmet. The steel armor protects their whole body.

Black: It lures people in with its Poké Ball pattern, then releases poison spores. Why it resembles a Poké Ball is unknown.\n\nWhite: For some reason, this Pokémon resembles a Poké Ball. They release poison spores to repel those who try to catch them.

Black: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.\n\nWhite: They show off their Poké Ball caps to lure prey, but very few Pokémon are fooled by this.

Black: With its thin, veil-like arms wrapped around the body of its opponent, it sinks to the ocean floor.\n\nWhite: They paralyze prey with poison, then drag them down to their lairs, five miles below the surface.

Black: The fate of the ships and crew that wander into Jellicent’s habitat: all sunken, all lost, all vanished.\n\nWhite: They propel themselves by expelling absorbed seawater from their bodies. Their favorite food is life energy.

Black: The special membrane enveloping Alomomola has the ability to heal wounds.\n\nWhite: Floating in the open sea is how they live. When they find a wounded Pokémon, they embrace it and bring it to shore.

Black: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.\n\nWhite: They attach themselves to large-bodied Pokémon and absorb static electricity, which they store in an electric pouch.

Black: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.\n\nWhite: They employ an electrically charged web to trap their prey. While it is immobilized by shock, they leisurely consume it.

Black: When threatened, it attacks by shooting a barrage of spikes, which gives it a chance to escape by rolling away.\n\nWhite: They stick their spikes into cave walls and absorb the minerals they find in the rock.

Black: It fights by swinging around its three spiky feelers. A hit from these steel spikes can reduce a boulder to rubble.\n\nWhite: They attach themselves to cave ceilings, firing steel spikes at targets passing beneath them.

Black: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.\n\nWhite: Interlocking two bodies and spinning around generates the energy they need to live.

Black: By changing the direction in which it rotates, it communicates its feelings to others. When angry, it rotates faster.\n\nWhite: Spinning minigears are rotated at high speed and repeatedly fired away. It is dangerous if the gears don’t return.
Black: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.\n\nWhite: The gear with the red core is rotated at high speed for a rapid energy charge.

Black: While one alone doesn’t have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.\n\nWhite: These Pokémon move in schools. They have an electricity-generating organ, so they discharge electricity if in danger.

Black: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.\n\nWhite: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

Black: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.\n\nWhite: With their sucker mouths, they suck in prey. Then they use their fangs to shock the prey with electricity.

Black: It uses its strong psychic power to squeeze its opponent’s brain, causing unendurable headaches.\n\nWhite: This Pokémon had never been seen until it appeared from far in the desert 50 years ago.

Black: It can manipulate an opponent’s memory. Apparently, it communicates by flashing its three different-colored fingers.\n\nWhite: It uses psychic power to control an opponent’s brain and tamper with its memories.

Black: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.\n\nWhite: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life force of any who follow it.
Black: This ominous Pokémon is feared. Through cities it wanders, searching for the spirits of the fallen.\n\nWhite: It arrives near the moment of death and steals spirit from the body.

Black: It absorbs a spirit, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.\n\nWhite: Being consumed in Chandelure’s flame burns up the spirit, leaving the body behind.

Black: They use their tusks to crush the berries they eat. Repeated regrowth makes their tusks strong and sharp.\n\nWhite: They mark their territory by leaving gashes in trees with their tusks. If a tusk breaks, a new one grows in quickly.

Black: Since a broken tusk will not grow back, they diligently sharpen their tusks on river rocks after they’ve been fighting.\n\nWhite: Their tusks can shatter rocks. Territory battles between Fraxure can be intensely violent.

Black: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.\n\nWhite: Their sturdy tusks will stay sharp even if used to cut steel beams. These Pokémon are covered in hard armor.

Black: When it is not feeling well, its mucus gets watery and the power of its Ice-type moves decreases.\n\nWhite: Its nose is always running. It sniffs the snot back up because the mucus provides the raw material for its moves.

Black: It can make its breath freeze at will. Very able in the water, it swims around in northern seas and catches prey.\n\nWhite: It freezes its breath to create fangs and claws of ice to fight with. Cold northern areas are its habitat.

Black: When its body temperature goes up, it turns into steam and vanishes. When its temperature lowers, it returns to ice.\n\nWhite: They are born in snow clouds. They use chains made of ice crystals to capture prey.

column2: Route 8, Icirrus City, Moor of Icirrus
column3: Black: When attacked, it defends itself by closing the lid of its shell. It can spit a sticky, poisonous liquid.\n\nWhite: It evolves when bathed in an electric-like energy along with Karrablast. The reason is still unknown.

Black: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.\n\nWhite: Having removed its heavy shell, it becomes very light and can fight with ninja-like movements.

column2: Route 8, Icirrus City, Moor of Icirrus
column3: Black: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.\n\nWhite: It conceals itself in the mud of the seashore. Then it waits. When prey touch it, it delivers a jolt of electricity.

Black: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.\n\nWhite: They have mastered elegant combos. As they concentrate, their battle moves become swifter and more precise.

Black: It wields the fur on its arms like a whip. Its arm attacks come with such rapidity that they cannot even be seen.\n\nWhite: They use the long fur on their arms as a whip to strike their opponents.

Black: It warms its body by absorbing sunlight with its wings. When its body temperature falls, it can no longer move.\n\nWhite: It races through narrow caves, using its sharp claws to catch prey. The skin on its face is harder than a rock.

Black: The energy that burns inside it enables it to move, but no one has yet been able to identify this energy.\n\nWhite: These Pokémon are thought to have been created by the science of an ancient and mysterious civilization.

Black: It flies across the sky at Mach speeds. Removing the seal on its chest makes its internal energy go out of control.\n\nWhite: It is said that Golurk were ordered to protect people and Pokémon by the ancient people who made them.

Black: Blades comprise this Pokémon’s entire body. If battling dulls the blades, it sharpens them on stones by the river.\n\nWhite: They fight at Bisharp’s command. They cling to their prey and inflict damage by sinking their blades into it.

Black: It leads a group of Pawniard. It battles to become the boss, but will be driven from the group if it loses.\n\nWhite: Bisharp pursues prey in the company of a large group of Pawniard. Then Bisharp finishes off the prey.

Black: Their fluffy fur absorbs damage, even if they strike foes with a fierce headbutt.\n\nWhite: They charge wildly and headbutt everything. Their headbutts have enough destructive force to derail a train.

Black: They crush berries with their talons. They bravely stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong it is.\n\nWhite: They will challenge anything, even strong opponents, without fear. Their frequent fights help them become stronger.

Black: They fight for their friends without any thought about danger to themselves. One can carry a car while flying.\n\nWhite: The more scars they have, the more respect these brave soldiers of the sky get from their peers.

Black: Its wings are too tiny to allow it to fly. As the time approaches for it to evolve, it discards the bones it was wearing.\n\nWhite: They tend to guard their posteriors with suitable bones they have found. They pursue weak Pokémon.

Black: It makes a nest out of bones it finds. It grabs weakened prey in its talons and hauls it to its nest of bones.\n\nWhite: Watching from the sky, they swoop to strike weakened Pokémon on the ground. They decorate themselves with bones.

Black: It breathes through a hole in its tail while it burns with an internal fire. Durant is its prey.\n\nWhite: Using their very hot, flame-covered tongues, they burn through Durant’s steel bodies and consume their insides.

Black: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.\n\nWhite: Durant dig nests in mountains. They build their complicated, interconnected tunnels into mazes.

Black: It tends to bite everything, and it is not a picky eater. Approaching it carelessly is dangerous.\n\nWhite: They cannot see, so they tackle and bite to learn about their surroundings. Their bodies are covered in wounds.

Black: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.\n\nWhite: Since their two heads do not get along and compete with each other for food, they always eat too much.

Black: This brutal Pokémon travels the skies on its six wings. Anything that moves seems like a foe to it, triggering its attack.\n\nWhite: The heads on their arms do not have brains. They use all three heads to consume and destroy everything.

Black: This Pokémon was believed to have been born from the sun. When it evolves, its entire body is engulfed in flames.\n\nWhite: The base of volcanoes is where they make their homes. They shoot fire from their five horns to repel attacking enemies.

Black: When volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere, it is said that Volcarona’s fire provided a replacement for the sun.\n\nWhite: A sea of fire engulfs the surroundings of their battles, since they use their six wings to scatter their ember scales.

Black: This legendary Pokémon battled against humans to protect Pokémon. Its personality is calm and composed.\n\nWhite: It has a body and heart of steel. Its glare is sufficient to make even an unruly Pokémon obey it.

Black: This Pokémon came to the defense of Pokémon that had lost their homes in a war among humans.\n\nWhite: Its charge is strong enough to break through a giant castle wall in one blow. This Pokémon is spoken of in legends.

Black: This Pokémon fought humans in order to protect its friends. Legends about it continue to be passed down.\n\nWhite: Its head sprouts horns as sharp as blades. Using whirlwind-like movements, it confounds and swiftly cuts opponents.

Black: The lower half of its body is wrapped in a cloud of energy. It zooms through the sky at 200 mph.\n\nWhite: Tornadus expels massive energy from its tail, causing severe storms. Its power is great enough to blow houses away.

Black: Countless charred remains mar the landscape of places through which Thundurus has passed.\n\nWhite: The spikes on its tail discharge immense bolts of lightning. It flies around the Unova region firing off lightning bolts.

Black: This Pokémon appears in legends. It sends flames into the air from its tail, burning up everything around it.\n\nWhite: When Reshiram’s tail flares, the heat energy moves the atmosphere and changes the world’s weather.

Black: Concealing itself in lightning clouds, it flies throughout the Unova region. It creates electricity in its tail.\n\nWhite: This Pokémon appears in legends. In its tail, it has a giant generator that creates electricity.

Black: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”\n\nWhite: The energy that comes pouring from its tail increases the nutrition in the soil, making crops grow to great size.
Black: It generates a powerful, freezing energy inside itself, but its body became frozen when the energy leaked out.\n\nWhite: It can produce ultracold air. Its body is frozen.

Black: By blasting water from its hooves, it can glide across water. It excels at using leg moves while battling.\n\nWhite: It crosses the world, running over the surfaces of oceans and rivers. It appears at scenic waterfronts.
Black: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.\n\nWhite: Many famous songs have been inspired by the melodies that Meloetta plays.

Black: Over 300 million years ago, it was feared as the strongest of hunters. It has been modified by Team Plasma.\n\nWhite: This ancient bug Pokémon was altered by Team Plasma. They upgraded the cannon on its back.
